headline: BNP MP Jilani’s house set on fire in Tungipara as attackers chant ‘Joy Bangla’

members.title: Banned Awami League men set Tungipara police station on fire
members.lead: Leaders and activists of the banned Awami League and its student wing, Bangladesh Chhatra League, whose activities are now banned, attacked and set fire to Tungipara police station in Gopalganj on Tuesday evening. After gathering in a procession, they first surrounded the police station and later attacked it and set fire to several vehicles inside its premises. Police reportedly fired tear gas shells, rubber bullets and sound grenades to bring the situation under control. Local sources said tension gripped the area after reports spread that police had detained several leaders and activists of the Awami League. Later, people were mobilised through an announcement over a mosque loudspeaker. At one point, they surrounded Tungipara police station and subsequently set it on fire. . Several videos of the attack and arson at the police station have circulated on Facebook. In one video, at least three vehicles can be seen burning inside the police station compound. Sounds of vandalism can also be heard. At the same time, the attackers were heard chanting slogans of “Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu”. Some of them were carrying sticks, while others were recording the attack and arson on their mobile phones. . In another video, a man identified as HM Rubel Farazi was heard saying during a Facebook Live broadcast, “We will set the police station on fire within a short time.” During the live broadcast, he also said police had fired tear gas at them. They were trying to extinguish the gas by lighting fires, he said, adding that they would not retreat. . Deputy Inspector General (Crime and Operations) of Police Headquarters Mohammad Abu Sufian told Prothom Alo over the phone at around 8:45pm on Tuesday that they had received reports that miscreants had surrounded Tungipara police station. They were making further inquiries to establish what had happened afterwards, he said. Later, at around 9:10pm, Prothom Alo contacted Police Headquarters spokesperson Kamarum Munira by phone. members.title: BNP MP Jilani’s house set on fire in Tungipara as attackers chant ‘Joy Bangla’
members.lead: Activists of the Awami League, whose activities are banned now, set fire to the house of SM Jilani, a lawmaker from Gopalganj-3 (Tungipara-Kotalipara) constituency and president of the central committee of Jatiyatabadi Swechchhasebak Dal, in Tungipara, Gopalganj, on Tuesday evening. Jilani’s house is about 1.5 kilometres from Tungipara police station. According to eyewitnesses and several BNP sources, the police station was set on fire first. Activists of the Awami League and its student wing, Bangladesh Chhatra League, subsequently attacked Jilani’s house, vandalised it and set it on fire. . Several videos of the attack on the lawmaker’s house have circulated on Facebook. One video shows flames engulfing different parts of the house, while a group of young men armed with sticks vandalise the interior. Some of them can be heard chanting ‘Joy Bangla’. One person is heard saying, “Jilani’s house is finished.” Prothom Alo tried several times to contact SM Jilani by phone but could not reach him. Sharif Rafiquzzaman, convener of Gopalganj district BNP, told Prothom Alo after 10pm, “I have heard from various sources that the house of lawmaker SM Jilani has been set on fire.”
